steps.title: Define the core concepts of data-intensive applications
steps.instruction: Create a function named defineDataIntensiveCharacteristics that returns a string describing the key characteristics of data-intensive applications.
steps.hint: Think about what makes an application data-intensive: large amounts of data, high speed of data flow, different types of data, and system requirements.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named defineDataIntensiveCharacteristics that returns a descriptive string about data-intensive application characteristics.
successCriteria: The function defineDataIntensiveCharacteristics exists and returns a string mentioning volume, velocity, variety, reliability, scalability, or maintainability.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the core characteristics of data-intensive applications.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it returns a string describing data-intensive application characteristics.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a function named defineDataIntensiveCharacteristics that returns a string about data-intensive apps.

steps.title: Identify the key components of a data-intensive system
steps.instruction: Create a function named identifySystemComponents that returns a list of the four essential components: data storage, data processing, data serving, and data ingestion.
steps.hint: Define a function that returns an array of strings containing the four component names.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function that returns an array containing the four key components of a data-intensive system.
successCriteria: The function identifySystemComponents exists and returns an array with exactly four strings: data storage, data processing, data serving, and data ingestion.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've correctly identified the four fundamental building blocks of a data-intensive system.
steps.feedbackPartial: You have some components, but check that you've included all four: data storage, data processing, data serving, and data ingestion.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function doesn't return the expected four components. Review the essential building blocks of data-intensive systems.

steps.title: Design the data storage layer
steps.instruction: Create a function named designStorageLayer that returns an object describing storage solutions for different data types.
steps.hint: The function should return an object with keys for different storage types and their appropriate use cases.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function that returns an object with storage solutions for structured, unstructured, and large file data.
successCriteria: The designStorageLayer function exists and returns an object with at least three storage type properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a function that will help design the storage layer by returning appropriate storage solutions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it returns an object describing storage solutions for different data types.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a function named designStorageLayer that returns an object with storage solutions.

steps.title: Design the data processing layer
steps.instruction: Create a function named designProcessingLayer that returns an object describing two processing approaches: batch processing and stream processing.
steps.hint: Define a function that returns an object with two properties, each describing a processing approach and its typical use case.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function that returns an object with batch and stream processing details.
successCriteria: The designProcessingLayer function exists and returns an object with batchProcessing and streamProcessing properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the data processing layer function. This establishes the foundation for implementing both batch and stream processing approaches.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the function, but make sure it returns an object with both batchProcessing and streamProcessing properties describing the approaches.
steps.feedbackWrong: The processing layer function isn't properly defined. Create a function named designProcessingLayer that returns an object with batch and stream processing details.

steps.title: Design the data serving layer
steps.instruction: Create a function named designServingLayer that returns a string describing the serving layer components.
steps.hint: Define a function that returns a string mentioning APIs and caching strategies.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named designServingLayer that returns a string describing APIs and caching strategies for data access.
successCriteria: The function designServingLayer is defined and returns a string containing 'API' and 'cache'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the serving layer design function. This function will describe how processed data is made available to users and applications through APIs and caching.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function is named exactly 'designServingLayer' and returns a string that mentions both APIs and caching strategies.
steps.feedbackWrong: The serving layer function isn't quite right. Create a function named designServingLayer that returns a descriptive string about APIs and caching.

steps.title: Design the data ingestion layer
steps.instruction: Create a function named designIngestionLayer that returns a string describing a data ingestion pipeline using message queues or ETL processes.
steps.hint: Define a function that returns a descriptive string about handling incoming data from multiple sources.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named designIngestionLayer is created that returns a string describing data ingestion pipelines.
successCriteria: The function designIngestionLayer exists and returns a string containing terms like 'message queue', 'ETL', or 'data ingestion'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the data ingestion layer function. This represents the component that handles incoming data from various sources.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it's named exactly 'designIngestionLayer' and returns a descriptive string about data ingestion.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function wasn't created correctly. Create a function named designIngestionLayer that returns a string describing data ingestion pipelines.

steps.title: Implement scalability patterns
steps.instruction: Create a function named implementScalabilityPatterns that returns an array containing the four scalability techniques: 'horizontal scaling', 'vertical scaling', 'sharding', and 'replication'.
steps.hint: Define a function that returns an array of strings. The order of the techniques should match the instruction.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new function implementScalabilityPatterns is defined, returning an array with the four scalability techniques.
successCriteria: The implementScalabilityPatterns function exists and returns an array containing exactly 'horizontal scaling', 'vertical scaling', 'sharding', and 'replication'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the scalability patterns function, which is crucial for designing systems that can handle growth in data and users.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the function may be missing some scalability techniques or the array order doesn't match. Ensure it returns all four techniques exactly as specified.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't implemented correctly. Make sure to create a function named implementScalabilityPatterns that returns an array with the four scalability techniques.

steps.title: Implement reliability patterns
steps.instruction: Create a function named implementReliabilityPatterns that returns a string describing reliability patterns for data-intensive systems.
steps.hint: Define a function with the given name that returns a descriptive string about redundancy, failover, backups, or monitoring.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named implementReliabilityPatterns is defined and returns a string about reliability patterns.
successCriteria: The implementReliabilityPatterns function exists and returns a string describing at least one reliability pattern (e.g., redundancy, failover, backups, monitoring).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've implemented a function for reliability patterns, which is crucial for ensuring system availability and data durability in data-intensive applications.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the function, but make sure it returns a descriptive string about reliability patterns like redundancy or failover.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't defined correctly. Create a function named implementReliabilityPatterns that returns a string describing reliability patterns.

steps.title: Design for maintainability
steps.instruction: Create a function named designForMaintainability that applies maintainability principles: modular design, clear documentation, automated testing, version control, and continuous integration/deployment pipelines.
steps.hint: Define a function that returns an array or object describing these maintainability principles.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named designForMaintainability is created that returns maintainability principles.
successCriteria: The designForMaintainability function exists and returns principles like modular design, documentation, testing, version control, and CI/CD.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the maintainability design function, which is essential for building systems that are easy to understand, modify, and extend over time.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it's named designForMaintainability and returns the key maintainability principles mentioned in the instruction.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is missing or doesn't match the required name and principles. Review the instruction to create a function named designForMaintainability that returns maintainability principles.

steps.title: Review and optimize the complete design
steps.instruction: Create a function named reviewAndOptimizeDesign that returns a string summarizing the design review process.
steps.hint: Define a function that returns a descriptive string about evaluating the system design.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named reviewAndOptimizeDesign is created that returns a string describing the design review process.
successCriteria: The function reviewAndOptimizeDesign is defined and returns a string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the review function, completing the system design process.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it's named exactly 'reviewAndOptimizeDesign' and returns a string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is not properly defined. Create a function named reviewAndOptimizeDesign that returns a string.
